summary: Created a local CA "OS Comparison Root CA" on node1 (RHEL7) via openssl, installed its certificate into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and ran update-ca-trust extract to register it as a trusted system CA. Verified trust functionally by issuing a test leaf certificate and confirming openssl verify accepted it against the system default trust store. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured a pre-restart boot_id and healthy-trust baseline, rebooted node1 via shutdown -r now, polled until exec access returned, confirmed the boot_id changed, and re-verified the CA anchor file, trust-list entry, ca-bundle inclusion, and end-to-end leaf-certificate verification all recovered post-reboot.
actions_performed: Confirmed node1 OS (RHEL 7.9) and tool availability (openssl, update-ca-trust, sudo -n)
Generated 4096-bit RSA key and self-signed x509 root CA cert with CN=O="OS Comparison Root CA", 10-year validity, in ~/os-comparison-ca
Copied CA cert to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/osCompRootCA.pem via sudo and ran update-ca-trust extract
Verified CA appears in trust list --filter=ca-anchors and in /etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt
Issued a test leaf certificate signed by the new CA and confirmed openssl verify succeeds against the system default trust store
Removed test leaf cert/key/csr files, keeping only the CA key/cert
Captured pre-restart boot_id (e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf) and re-confirmed CA trust health as baseline
Restarted node1 via sudo shutdown -r now (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec access returned; observed connection timeout during reboot, then success
Confirmed new boot_id (d636db92-d369-4039-8006-cc1153b25695), proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart: re-verified CA anchor file, trust-list entry, ca-bundle inclusion, and issued+verified a fresh leaf certificate against the system trust store

evidence.requirement: CA created with correct name (OS Comparison Root CA) and installed as a trusted system CA on node1
evidence.summary: openssl generated the CA key/cert with subject CN=O="OS Comparison Root CA"; it was copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and update-ca-trust extract was run; trust list and ca-bundle.crt confirm registration; a leaf cert signed by this CA verified OK against the system default trust store, proving functional system-wide trust.
Captured boot_id e9250ad1-c4f0-4bec-b58e-4e30255a8dcf and confirmed the CA anchor file verifies OK and is present in trust list before restart.

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement and execution unavailability during reboot
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now was issued in background so the ack returned immediately; the very next poll timed out connecting to node1, consistent with an in-progress reboot.

evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Post-reboot poll succeeded and returned a new boot_id (d636db92-d369-4039-8006-cc1153b25695), differing from the pre-restart boot_id, and a fresh uptime -s timestamp.

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of required services/data (CA trust)
evidence.summary: After reboot, the CA anchor file, trust list entry, and ca-bundle.crt inclusion were all still present, and a newly issued leaf certificate verified OK against the system trust store, proving the CA trust configuration survived and functions correctly post-restart.
